profile.campus: AWS Northern Indiana campus, New Carlisle, St. Joseph County
profile.address: Western Avenue, Saint Joseph County, Indiana, 46552
profile.reading:
This building is one of the data center structures Amazon Web Services operates near New Carlisle in St. Joseph County, Indiana, part of AWS's Northern Indiana data center campus near South Bend. AWS and Indiana state officials announced the original investment in this campus, put at $11 billion, in 2024; the Indianapolis Business Journal, DataCenterDynamics, and Inside INdiana Business all covered the announcement, and Amazon later broke ground on the campus per Northwest Indiana Business Magazine's coverage of the groundbreaking. On November 24, 2025, Amazon announced on its own aboutamazon.com news page a further $15 billion investment in Northern Indiana data center campuses, on top of the earlier commitment, framed as adding up to 2.4 gigawatts of data center capacity to the region, with a further gigawatt of grid capacity beyond Amazon's own needs also planned. Amazon's release put the new investment at generating roughly 1,100 new high-skilled direct jobs plus thousands of additional supply-chain jobs in construction, electrical work, and fiber-optic technician roles, and said the added grid capacity was projected to save existing Indiana households and businesses about $1 billion in electricity costs over 15 years. Amazon's release also disclosed that its cumulative investment in Indiana across all business lines, including its data centers, fulfillment network, and delivery stations, had exceeded $31.3 billion since 2010, supporting an estimated 24,500 direct and 27,500 indirect jobs and contributing more than $29.9 billion to the state's economy.

AWS has not published a street address, opening date, floor area, or an IT power rating specific to this individual building distinct from the regional gigawatt figures disclosed for the Northern Indiana campus as a whole, and no source found for this page breaks that campus down building by building.

profile.capacity_note: Not published at the individual building level. Amazon's own aboutamazon.com release describes the Northern Indiana campus in aggregate: up to 2.4 gigawatts of data center capacity from the newest phase of investment, plus additional grid capacity, without assigning megawatt or square footage figures to specific buildings.
profile.facility_note: AWS has not identified this specific building by name, construction date, or function in any source found for this page. It is treated as part of the documented AWS St. Joseph County / New Carlisle campus described above.

profile.regional_context: St. Joseph County, Indiana, anchored by New Carlisle near South Bend, became a hyperscale data center location only recently, with AWS's initial $11 billion campus announcement in 2024 followed by a further $15 billion commitment in November 2025. Amazon's own materials tie the expansion directly to regional grid capacity, stating the buildout adds gigawatt-scale capacity to the local power system, part of which Amazon says is intended to benefit other Indiana electricity customers rather than serve AWS alone. Indiana's state government has actively courted large data center investment through economic development incentives covered by Inside INdiana Business and the Indianapolis Business Journal, and has positioned the AWS campus alongside the state's broader push to attract large-load industrial and technology investment to areas outside its traditional manufacturing base.

reading.body:
Amazon Web Services operates this facility in St. Joseph County as part of its cloud infrastructure, but does not publish specific power capacity, square footage, or other technical specifications for individual data centers as a matter of company policy. The operator discloses only that each AWS region contains a minimum of three physically separate availability zones with independent power and cooling, without breaking capacity down to individual site level. This disclosure policy applies across all AWS facilities and is not specific to this location.

Indiana hosts six mapped data center facilities, of which two operators have published power figures totaling 22.5 megawatts. This AWS facility ranks third among the state's published capacity, though its own capacity is not published. The state holds no detailed power or grid information for this site beyond its geographic coordinates and operator identity.

Without published specifications, this facility cannot be assessed for its contribution to AI scaling constraints in Indiana or ranked against other major compute campuses. The absence of disclosed capacity figures reflects AWS's security practice and does not indicate the facility's scale or significance to regional power demand.
